newsitem.title: USA: Aluminum destocking over, market balanced -Spector.
newsitem.headline: Aluminum destocking over, market balanced -Spector.

text.p: Preliminary data for the first quarter suggested that following the end of destocking, aluminum market supply and demand were back in balance, industry analyst Stewart Spector said in his latest Aluminum Industry Service report.

"With the end of destocking by end-users, the resurgence in world economic activity, and the declining trend in primary inventories, stocks could fall below desired levels in the current quarter," Spector said.
Western world ingot inventories, both visible and estimated unreported, now approximate 3.1 million tons or 1.9 months of supply, Spector added.
This is down 600,000 tons from a high of 3.7 million tons and 2.7 months of supply in January last year.
"Relative to demand, producers' ingot stocks are now at their lowest level on record," Spector said.

Aluminum orders and backlogs are on the upswing and integrated producers need to buy back metal units to make fabricated products. LME and unreported stocks will now flow back to the mills, Spector added.
"To bring the supply system back into balance, the remaining idle capacity could be restarted in the third and fourth quarter of this year," Spector said.
